```
JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64 bazelisk --host_jvm_args '-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=/etc/ssl/certs/java/cacerts' build --host_javabase '@local_jdk//:jdk' //mytarget```

when add custom cert by keytool `keytool -import -alias ca -keystore /root/.cache/bazel/_bazel_root/install/a4696acfbd71b79376c811717f94d1ac/_embedded_binaries/embedded_tools/jdk/lib/security/cacerts -file /root/ca.cer`, it will cause `FATAL: corrupt installation: file '/root/.cache/bazel/_bazel_root/install/a4696acfbd71b79376c811717f94d1ac/_embedded_binaries/embedded_tools/jdk/lib/security/cacerts' is missing or modified.  Please remove '/root/.cache/bazel/_bazel_root/install/a4696acfbd71b79376c811717f94d1ac' and try again.` error.

> when add custom cert by keytool `keytool -import -alias ca -keystore /root/.cache/bazel/_bazel_root/install/a4696acfbd71b79376c811717f94d1ac/_embedded_binaries/embedded_tools/jdk/lib/security/cacerts -file /root/ca.cer`, it will cause `FATAL: corrupt installation: file '/root/.cache/bazel/_bazel_root/install/a4696acfbd71b79376c811717f94d1ac/_embedded_binaries/embedded_tools/jdk/lib/security/cacerts' is missing or modified. Please remove '/root/.cache/bazel/_bazel_root/install/a4696acfbd71b79376c811717f94d1ac' and try again.` error.

using `touch -m -c -r blacklisted.certs cacerts` change the file attr, still valid certification failed.

Same problem on RHEL7. Guess there aren't too many of us on the internet using Bazel behind an SSL gateway. We typically symlink `cacerts` to the one which is updated with ca-certificates on Red Hat images with our custom SSL certs.

Similar issue is #5741.

That issue contains a clean [workaround](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/5741#issuecomment-418071387) that is still valid for Ubuntu 20 and Bazel 4.0.0. That is, in your `.bazelrc` add:

```
startup --host_jvm_args=-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=/etc/ssl/certs/java/cacerts \
        --host_jvm_args=-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword=changeit
```
It seems bazel doesn't honor any certificate outside the default java store even using the above .bazelrc configs. Is this the case ? or any workaround i can leverage ?

issue.title: Use the system trust store by default with the embedded JDK

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
Users can't easily update the certificates in the embedded JDK and arguably shouldn't even have to be aware of the fact that Bazel relies on a bundled JVM. Since JDK 23 made it possible to rely on the system store on all major OSes, do so by default.

RELNOTES[INC]: Bazel releases that include a bundled JDK now use the system trust store for certificates by default. Set `-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore` and `-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStoreType` via `--host_jvm_args` to override the default location.

Fixes #16223 
Fixes #10349
